html:
This is the map's label for the united Korean kingdom from 1000 to 1900, under two long dynasties, Goryeo and Joseon. Korea had been mostly united since Unified Silla in the 600s.

Goryeo (918 to 1392). Wang Geon founded Goryeo in 918 and reunited the peninsula by 936; its name became the English "Korea". It was a Buddhist, aristocratic state, famous for celadon pottery. From 1231 the Mongols invaded again and again. While the court held out on Ganghwa Island, monks carved the more than 80,000 woodblocks of the Tripitaka Koreana. Korea then became a subordinate ally of the Yuan. In 1377 Korean printers made the Jikji, the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type.

Joseon (1392 to 1897). General Yi Seong-gye seized power and founded Joseon, with its capital at Hanyang, now Seoul. It was a strict Confucian state. Its peak came under Sejong the Great, who had the Hangul alphabet created in the 1440s. Japan invaded in the Imjin War of 1592 to 1598; Admiral Yi Sun-sin and Ming armies helped drive them out. Manchu invasions in 1627 and 1636 forced Joseon to submit to the Qing.

After that Joseon limited contact with the outside world and was called the Hermit Kingdom. Japan forced it open with the Treaty of Ganghwa in 1876. The Korean Empire, declared in 1897, became a Japanese protectorate in 1905 and was annexed in 1910.
